Clinical samples from patients with confirmed ANDV, collected between March 9, 2011, and June 27, 2024, were analysed and sequenced. Consensus sequences for the S, M, and L segments were generated, and genetic clustering and divergence were assessed using phylogenetic inference and variant calling. analysis.summary_en: There are two major clinical syndromes associated with human infections: hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) — mostly reported from Europe and Asia, and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) — mostly reported from the Americas. title: Modeling the Transmission Dynamics of Hantavirus with Environmental Viral Persistence

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hantavirus is a zoonotic infection maintained principally in rodent reservoirs, and human exposure occurs mainly through environments contaminated with infectious viral particles.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study formulates and analyses a deterministic compartmental model for hantavirus transmission involving susceptible and infected rodents, susceptible, exposed, infectious and recovered humans, and an environmental viral reservoir.
analysis.methods: The disease-free equilibrium is obtained, and the basic reproduction number is derived using the next-generation matrix method.
analysis.main_results: Stability analysis shows that the disease-free equilibrium is locally and globally asymptotically stable when R0 < 1, whereas disease persistence is associated with R0 > 1 and the existence of a biologically feasible endemic equilibrium.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings suggest that reducing rodent infection, limiting environmental contamination and increasing viral clearance may help move the system below the epidemic threshold.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The analysis indicates that environmental viral persistence provides an indirect pathway that can sustain transmission between infected rodents, susceptible rodents and humans.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The model offers a mathematically tractable framework for interpreting hantavirus persistence and for guiding future extensions involving seasonality, spatial structure, stochasticity and data-driven parameterisation.

analysis.summary_en: Hantavirus is a zoonotic infection maintained principally in rodent reservoirs, and human exposure occurs mainly through environments contaminated with infectious viral particles. This study formulates and analyses a deterministic compartmental model for hantavirus transmission involving susceptible and infected rodents, susceptible, exposed, infectious and recovered humans, and an environmental viral reservoir. The disease-free equilibrium is obtained, and the basic reproduction number is derived using the next-generation matrix method. Stability analysis shows that the disease-free equilibrium is locally and globally asymptotically stable when R0 < 1, whereas disease persistence is associated with R0 > 1 and the existence of a biologically feasible endemic equilibrium. These findings suggest that reducing rodent infection, limiting environmental contamination and increasing viral clearance may help move the system below the epidemic threshold. The analysis indicates that environmental viral persistence provides an indirect pathway that can sustain transmission between infected rodents, susceptible rodents and humans. The model offers a mathematically tractable framework for interpreting hantavirus persistence and for guiding future extensions involving seasonality, spatial structure, stochasticity and data-driven parameterisation.

analysis.summary_en: However, the preparation of these strips is time-consuming and labor-intensive. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the long-term storage conditions for the developed multiplex ICA strips. Therefore, we have previously developed a multiplex immunochromatographic assay (ICA) to detect antibodies against six pathogens as follows: mouse hepatitis virus, Sendai virus, and Clostridium piliforme (Tyzzer's disease) in mice, and Seoul type orthohantavirus, Sendai virus, and sialodacryoadenitis virus in rats. However, when stored at 18-28 °C (room temperature) and 4 °C, the detectable reactivity of the multiplex ICA strips stored in poly_bags was reduced for some of the six targets pathogens at 18 months after storage. The oxygen absorber reduced detectability of the multiplex ICA strips. Serological monitoring of infectious diseases in laboratory rodents is vital for ensuring animal health. These results indicate that storing ICA strips in poly_bags at -30 °C, which is a simple method, is able to maintain detectability long-term for the strips format and pathogen targets examined in this study.

In this study, a mathematical modeling framework—including compartmental, small-world (SW), and scale-free (SF) network models—was developed to analyze the dynamics of hantavirus and norovirus transmission on recent cruise ship outbreaks. The results show that when the initial number of exposed or infected individuals is extremely small (e.g., 1–2 persons), disease spread is dominated by stochasticity, causing substantial variation between individual simulations and mean model predictions.
